newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast products weaken amid lack of buyers.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast products weaken amid lack of buyers.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot refined products markets were steady to weaker in terribly thin trade Wednesday that was punctuated by a terribly neutral stocks report toward the end of the day, traders said.

Some traders had said in the early going that waiting ahead of the American Petroleum Institute's (API) weekly data was sapping the market of liquidity, but the report's arrival did nothing to give the market life.
API said West Coast crude stocks rose last week by 122,000 barrels to 62 million.
Gasoline stocks meanwhile fell by 166,000 barrels to 29.4 million barrels and distillate stocks fell by 224,000 barrels to 11.7 million barrels, according to API.
Regular CARB-grade cleaner burning gasoline was heard done in San Francisco ahead of the report at 62 cents a gallon, but that price was notionally weaker after the API data's arrival.
"There are some bids but no buyers," said one trader.
Regular CARB gasoline in Los Angeles was fetching between 62 and 63 cents late Wednesday -- perhaps a cent firmer than in San Francisco, traders said.
Regular unleaded gasoline in Los Angeles was pegged at between 60 and 61 cents a gallon -- also a cent firmer than in the Bay Area.
On the distillate front, prices in Los Angeles were also about a cent firmer than in San Francisco, with CARB-grade low sulphur, low aromatic diesel pegged in LA at between 64 and 65 cents a gallon.
EPA-grade diesel in LA stood between 58 and 59 cents a gallon -- again a cent firmer than in San Francisco.
-- Oliver Ludwig New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
